clue.text: Crustaceans manage when facing groups of whales

parts.note: to manage is to cope, get by
a pod is a group of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: Someone coping as they face down whole schools of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Copepods are tiny aquatic crustaceans, a staple of plankton that whales feed on.

clue.text: Church has second gentleman turning up for baptismal robe

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up reads the pieces backwards

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
sir is a polite title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A church gentleman arriving with the christening gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrisom is the white robe put on a child at baptism.

clue.text: Get rid of cherubic child without father and identity

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the child goes round the rest

parts.note: a putto is a cherub figure in Renaissance art
pa is father
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: Disposing of a cherub with neither dad nor papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a deletion signal but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: To put paid to something is to finish it off or end it for good.

clue.text: Those putting coats on horses

definitions.meaning: ... coat objects with a thin layer of metal
inferior racehorses that run in plate races

explanation.surface: People dressing horses in coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Plating is applying a metal coat; a plater is also a low-grade racehorse.

clue.text: Product on sale just before Christmas maybe to become less successful?

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the month leading up to Christmas
a line is a type of product a shop sells

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a pre-Christmas product will flop.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to deteriorate or fall away in fortune or strength.

clue.text: Bag is a pain, being left in street

indicators.note: something left in a place stays inside it, so the pain sits inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A bag dumped in the road becomes an annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed bag or packet, as of sugar or shampoo.

clue.text: Building given criticism — one university must replace

indicators.note: replacing means substituting, so the university letter goes in where the one was

parts.note: a stricture is a severe criticism
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A building criticised, and one university demanding a change.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure is something built, such as a building or bridge.

clue.text: Rushes to offer cold rather than hot dishes

indicators.note: rather than means instead of, so the cold letter is used in place of the hot one

parts.note: rushes means hurries
H is hot, as on a tap
C is cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Hurrying to serve chilled rather than hot food.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that curries are usually hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Curries are spiced dishes of meat or vegetables in a sauce.

clue.text: Width of river accommodating vessels

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the river holds the vessels

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A broad river with boats on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide, open area, a great breadth of land or water.

clue.text: Queen with fantastic cat, more than once her destroyer of rodents

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly imaginative, so the letters of cat are reshaped

parts.note: the word cat is used more than once, so it is written twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A queen whose fantastic pet cat is, again and again, the scourge of mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' doubles CAT and 'fantastic' rearranges CATCAT as ATCATC, framed by R and HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratcatcher is someone employed to kill or trap rats and similar vermin.

clue.text: Rhapsodic form of modern music, conclusion for concert

parts.note: rap is a modern musical genre

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, here of concert

explanation.surface: A modern rhapsody ends a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means wholly absorbed or enraptured, close to rhapsodic in its ecstatic delight.

clue.text: Decorating site for play — this tells theatre folk what to do

definitions.text: this tells theatre folk what to do

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dressing a set for a stage play, then a note for the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for play' reads as theatre talk, but 'play' is the anagram signal and 'for' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage direction is a written instruction in a script telling actors where to move or how to act.

clue.text: Swimmers used to swim in West?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed in the name, signalling insertion

parts.note: Mae West was an American film actress; her first name goes round the rest

indicators.note: swimming letters move about, so the word used is rearranged

explanation.surface: Swimmers who once swam out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' reads as a compass point, but the question mark hints at the film star Mae West; 'to swim' rearranges USED inside her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusae are jellyfish in their free-swimming bell-shaped stage.

clue.text: Get to meeting with old rocker disgraced at one time

parts.note: to attain a place is to get to it
a Ted, Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth fond of rock and roll

explanation.surface: Arriving at a gathering with an aging rock fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Attainted, an archaic legal term, meant stripped of rights after a conviction, so dishonoured.

clue.text: In the capacity of hut that has to be knocked down

parts.note: qua is Latin-derived English for in the capacity of
a shed is a hut

explanation.surface: A hut that is due for demolition.
explanation.definitionFit: To quash is to overturn or suppress, as a court quashes a verdict, so quashed is struck down.

clue.text: Unoriginal journo with requirement to be heard

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often a mediocre one

indicators.note: the requirement word is spoken, giving a sound spelt differently

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: A dull reporter who needs attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed means overused and stale, lacking freshness.

clue.text: Quiet diocese in which set of holy books is put forward

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quiet

indicators.note: the diocese has the books placed in it

parts.note: Rome is a diocese, the Pope's own see
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A peaceful diocese where scripture is advanced.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote is to advance or put forward a person, idea or product.

clue.text: Wrench restricting one part of body or another

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the wrench encloses the body part

parts.note: to rend is to wrench or tear apart
the ear is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A wrench clamping one bit of the body after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of body' does double duty: one part is EAR, the other part is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear end, the backside, is a second part of the body.

clue.text: Audible sound of farmyard animal close by makes one more dreamy

parts.note: moo is the sound a cow makes

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the words are spoken and the result spelt another way

parts.note: near means close by

explanation.surface: Mooing nearby sends someone into a daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: Moony means dreamy and absent-minded, so moonier is the comparative.

clue.text: Failure of young socialite star to seal deal finally

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young woman entering society

indicators.note: sealing means enclosing, so the star wraps the letter

parts.note: an ace is a star performer

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of deal

explanation.surface: A young socialite who is a star fails to close a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating collapse or fiasco.

clue.text: Driver of cart taking a road north — new girl going that way

indicators.note: in a down answer heading north means reading upwards, backwards
that way refers back to north, so these pieces are also reversed

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cart driver heading north on a road, with a new girl along the same route.
explanation.definitionFit: A drayman drives a dray, a low cart used especially for brewery deliveries.

clue.text: Guy in America, about 50, one rushing around

indicators.note: about means around, so the guy encloses the number

parts.note: buster is an American form of address to a man
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: An American man around fifty who is always busy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustler is someone who moves about energetically and fussily.

clue.text: Forces out former leftists after revolution

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Trots is short for Trotskyists, a far-left faction

explanation.surface: Ex-radicals forcibly ousted after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suits the leftists in the surface, but 'after revolution' is the anagram signal, making TORTS; Trots is a British nickname for Trotskyists.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to wrest money or concessions from someone by force or threats.

clue.text: Scientist builds up from this small amount — aims at miscount being corrected

definitions.text: Scientist builds up from this small amount

indicators.note: correcting a miscount puts things right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist's minute unit and someone's botched tally being put right.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic mass unit is the tiny standard unit for expressing the masses of atoms and molecules.

clue.text: One guided around shop

indicators.note: turning around signals the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
guided means led

explanation.surface: Someone shown round a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Unselfish group member: "Pay me later for working"

indicators.note: working means in operation, so these letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A staff member offering to be paid later for work done.
explanation.definitionFit: A team player puts the side's interests ahead of personal glory.

clue.text: A left-winger kept outside party much admired

indicators.note: the left-winger with the A is kept on the outside, around the party

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A socialist excluded from a gathering of cherished guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored means loved deeply, much more than merely admired.

clue.text: Home with jazzy style given huge architectural feature

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
trad is traditional jazz
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, so huge

explanation.surface: A house decorated in jazz style with something massive.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrados is the inner curve or underside of an arch, an architectural term.
